title: Wilbur Sweatman and the Lafayette Theatre
summary: Sweatman played several horns at once in a trio at Harlem's Lafayette Theatre; scale was $55 a week.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That's Big Chief Moore's tour, that I did with Big Chief.
You eventually got with Wilbur Sweatman.
In New York. Tell us how you got with Sweatman. And that was apparently... According to the information in Chilton, it was around 1928, and you stayed with him for about three years.

Well, I'd say between 1928 and '29. He used to use a trio all the time, piano, himself and drums. Butt he played three different instruments at one time, clarinet, oboe and another horn -- but he played three.
He played an oboe also? That's...
And the clarinet, and a bass...bass...
A bass... Oboe and something else.
A bassoon. He played all of them.
He was a good musician, too. So I worked with him at the Lafayette Theatre.
Yes. The Lafayette Theatre. He had a piano player. We was up on the stage, the piano...

In fact, he had two pianists. Two pianists. I forgot the girl's name now. She was a very good piano player. Anyway, we did... I worked with Wilbur Sweatman. During that time, we weren't getting no more than the scale. The scale was fifty-five dollars a week.
